answers-lazy.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Twenty of two thousand rows, abandoned, fifty times over. The inference pin is ZERO and that zero is the case: bridge.pl's metta_node_guarded/2 reports what a job spent as that job's LAST event, reached only once the command has no more answers, so an abandoned job contributes nothing. A lazy path that began draining would report query-rows' 282622 and fail this row by four orders of magnitude, and the workload's own crossing bound fails first at 1600. Instructions carry the SIZE, since a counter fixed at zero cannot say whether twenty rows cost twenty rows' work or two thousand; most of what they price is the teardown, because leaving the loop early closes the cursor and destroys the engine behind it. Fifty abandonments rather than one because a two millisecond window spread 0.2763 percent across nine samples against a one percent band. atom-intern.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Twenty thousand interned expressions, each minted twice so the run exercises the table's miss path and its hit path, with the `===` between them as the interning guarantee itself. Instructions decide and inferences are null because the engine is never asked: a pin of zero there could not be disturbed by any change to this code. Instructions spread 0.0027 percent over 9 samples of 3 consecutive runs. The one percent band is sized for code LAYOUT and not only for measurement noise: un-exporting one unused function from benchmarks/sampler.ts, which changes no behaviour this row reaches, moved it 3644544733 to 3635000141, minus 0.26 percent, which is forty times the run-to-run spread [measured 2026-08-28; see Mytkowicz et al., ASPLOS 2009, cited by the Python seat's own layout-mode rows] [measured 2026-08-28: minimum of [3635197025, 3635192583, 3635140262]; command=CHECK_PY=/home/user/Dev/.venv-pypetta/bin/python sh extensions/node/bench.sh --update; fixture=swipl-wasm 8.0.6 on node 22.22.1 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.35), the compiled TypeScript build, box under loadavg 9 with another gate running; commit=WORKTREE]

define-call.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Five hundred host calls of a lowered `define`d body, 477.01 inferences a call. The body is lowered, so the whole of it lives in the engine and a call costs no host crossing per step; what this prices is the per-call path, the ask out and the one answer back. Inferences alone decide, because the host's share is one ask per call and is already the smallest this door can be. host-op.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Two thousand yields of a generator operation the engine pulls one answer at a time, 40.61 inferences and 1.003 crossings a yield. The one workload here whose cost is genuinely SPLIT, so both counters are pinned and they decide different halves: foreign code retires no inferences, so the engine counter sees its own side of each crossing and none of this seat's. A change that moved work from the engine into the host would improve the inference row and leave the instruction row flat, which is what pinning both makes visible. query-rows.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Two thousand rows asked and drained through the thenable, 141.31 inferences and 1.0015 crossings a row. `await ans` hands off to toArray, which walks the same async iterator `for await` walks, so this is the EAGER half of the pair answers-lazy completes and the two are one workload consumed two ways. Inferences decide because the engine does the work; instructions are pinned beside them because the engine counter is blind to this seat's half of each answer, and a change that added a round trip per row would leave it untouched. counter_policy: stats().inferences minimum of three and fixed two-point growth slopes decide; wall time advises
counter_policy_note: Inferences decide wherever the engine does the work and are identical run to run; retired instructions decide where the work is on the TypeScript side of the wire, where the engine counter cannot move; three cases straddle the boundary and pin both. Wall clock decides NOTHING here and is recorded for advice only: every number in this file was taken on a box under loadavg 9 with another gate running, where the inference rows were byte identical across nine samples and wall clock was not.
instruction_policy: perf instructions:u minimum of three, one percent noise allowance unless a row declares its own beside the measurement that justified it
v8_flag_note: Every instructions row is measured under the v8_flags in the stamp. A Node process is not deterministic enough to gate on retired instructions without them: bare, one engine workload spread 29.48 percent over four rounds, --liftoff-only alone took it to 2.55 percent and named the mechanism as TurboFan tiering swipl-wasm up on background threads inside the window, and the full set reaches 0.027 percent. These rows therefore measure Liftoff-compiled WebAssembly and single-threaded V8 rather than the tier a long-lived process settles into, which is the right trade for a gate that reads the change [measured 2026-08-28].
